[Flaky Test Fixer] Open a draft fix PR for issues labeled `ai:auto-flaky-fix` (#268810)

This PR adds a new agentic workflow that fires when a `failed-test`
issue is labeled `ai:auto-flaky-fix`.

- It reads the latest Failed Test Investigator comment to pick up the
suspected root cause
- It applies the smallest test-side patch it can justify
- It verifies the fix locally and opens a draft PR labeled
`auto:flaky-fix` if successful.

> [!NOTE]
> As of today, we're expecting the `ai:auto-flaky-fix` label to me added
**manually** - as a next step, the failed test investigator workflow
will add the label once we're confident flaky test fix PRs quality is
good enough.

@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+---
+name: Flaky Test Fixer
+description: Open a draft fix PR for a `failed-test` issue that has been labeled `ai:auto-flaky-fix`.
+on:
+  issues:
+    types: [labeled]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      issue_number:
+        description: Issue number in this repository to fix
+        required: true
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+  actions: read
+  checks: read
+  models: read
+
+if: "${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.issue_number != '') || (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'ai:auto-flaky-fix' && !github.event.issue.pull_request) }}"
+
+concurrency:
+  group: 'flaky-test-fixer-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue_number }}'
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+env:
+  ISSUE_NUMBER: &issue_number ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue_number }}
+
+engine:
+  id: claude
+  version: '2.1.111'
+  model: opus
+  max-turns: 200
+  env:
+    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_API_KEY }}
+    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://elastic.litellm-prod.ai
+    ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H: '1'
+    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: llm-gateway/claude-opus-4-7[1m]
+    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: llm-gateway/claude-haiku-4-5
+    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: llm-gateway/claude-sonnet-4-6
+    CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: opus[1m]
+
+tools:
+  github:
+    toolsets: [default, search]
+  web-fetch:
+  bash:
+    [
+      'cat',
+      'head',
+      'tail',
+      'grep',
+      'wc',
+      'sort',
+      'uniq',
+      'date',
+      'yq',
+      'jq',
+      'echo',
+      'ls',
+      'pwd',
+      'git:*',
+      'gh:*',
+      'bk:*',
+      'node',
+      'yarn',
+      'curl',
+    ]
+
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - buildkite.com
+    - '*.buildkite.com'
+    - ci-stats.kibana.dev
+    - github.com
+    - api.github.com
+    - elastic.litellm-prod.ai
+sandbox:
+  agent: awf
+
+safe-outputs:
+  staged: true
+  activation-comments: false
+  report-failure-as-issue: false
+  add-comment:
+    max: 1
+    target: *issue_number
+    hide-older-comments: true
+  create-pull-request:
+    draft: true
+    max: 1
+    labels: [ai:flaky-fix-ready]
+    base-branch: main
+    allowed-base-branches: [main]
+    if-no-changes: 'ignore'
+    protected-files: fallback-to-issue
+
+strict: false
+timeout-minutes: 90
+---
+
+# Flaky Test Fixer
+
+Open one draft PR with the smallest test-side fix for this flaky-test issue. If you cannot find a credible fix, stop without opening a PR.
+
+## Steps
+
+1. Read the investigator's comment on the issue for the suspected root cause and proposed fix. If no action is needed, stop.
+2. Read the failing test and the helpers, fixtures, and page objects it imports.
+3. Apply the smallest test-side patch that addresses the root cause.
+4. Run the test locally until it passes.
+5. Open the PR (see "PR format" below).
+
+## PR format
+
+- **Title**: `[<Plugin name>] <concise summary of the fix>`. Derive the plugin name from the test file path (e.g. `x-pack/solutions/security/plugins/security_solution/...` → `Security Solution`).
+- **Body**:
+
+  ```
+  Fixes #<issue-number> (add more issue numbers here if this fix resolves multiple issues)
+
+  <a few sentences: what was failing, and what this patch changes>
+
+  #### Verified locally
+
+  <bullet list of what you successfully ran on this branch — e.g. `yarn kbn bootstrap`, `node scripts/check --profile agent`, the targeted test passed N times in a row, etc. Include the exact commands.>
+
+  #### Not verified locally
+
+  <bullet list of what you could not verify and why — e.g. behavior under CI parallel load, on a different stack version, against a real Elasticsearch instance, etc. Omit this section if there is nothing to mention.
+
+  This PR was opened automatically by the Flaky Test Fixer. Provide feedback in [#appex-qa](https://elastic.slack.com/archives/C04HT4P1YS3).
+  ```

[Flaky test fixer] Use `am` git patch mode to avoid unshallow timeout in safe outputs step (#273676)

I noticed the latest flaky test fixer `safe-outputs` step [timed
out](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/actions/runs/27675349698)
(causing the flaky fix PR not to be created for issue
https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/273615):

```
08:23:39.041  [command]/usr/bin/git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository
08:23:39.046  Repository is shallow; fetching full history before applying bundle
08:23:39.047  [command]/usr/bin/git fetch --unshallow origin
08:37:03.315  ##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

Error (find it in the job summary):

```
The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 15m0s
```

I learned the GitHub agentic workflow use the bundle patch transport (in
a repo like Kibana this is effectively a full clone: rather unnecessary
and time-consuming). Let's use the `am` patch format instead (it will
apply the patch with the `git am --3way` command, no full history
needed).

Learn more about how the PR creation process works in the
[docs](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/safe-outputs-pull-requests/#how-it-works).

[Flaky Test Fixer] Open fix PRs as kibanamachine and comment outcomes on the issue (#275884)

This PR makes the following changes:

1. [Trigger] The flaky test fixer workflow creates the flaky test fix PR
using `kibanamachine` (instead of the `github-actions` bot). This allows
for the subsequent flaky test verifier step to be triggered as a
downstream workflow.
2. [Trigger] We now trigger the test verifier workflow even if
developers add the `flaky-test-fixer` label. It will make testing flaky
test runner invocations easier to test; we'll revert it back.
3. [DX] The flaky test fixer workflow will now post a comment inside the
`failed-test` issue to let developers know if a PR was or was not
created.
4. [DX] We now mention the user who added the `ai:fix-flaky` label
within the issue comment and the PR body (so they get pinged as soon as
the PR is open) - we won't mention them if they're a bot.

---------

[Flaky Test Fixer] Bootstrap Kibana so the agent can type-check its fix (#276170)

This PR bootstraps Kibana so the flaky test fixer is able to lint and
type check its proposed fix:

* The boostrap step runs _before_ `awf` launches the sandboxed agent, so
it is not subject to the agent firewall and reaches the Yarn registry
and bazel cache natively.
* The sandboxed agent is then able to lint and type check its fix fully
offline against the already-installed `node_modules`.

I noticed the workflow sometimes produced PRs that don't compile because
of the missing linting / type checks, which developers had to fix
manually (or with Copilot):

* https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/276155 (`registry.yarnpkg.com`
blocked by firewall + owning team had to fix a syntax error)
* https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/275830 (`yarn kbn bootstrap
could not complete in this sandbox` under "Verification")

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

[Flaky Test Fixer] Link the fix PR URL in the outcome comment (#276404)

This PR updates the flaky test fixer agentic workflow so that it links
the draft fix PR directly in the comment it posts on `failed-test`
GitHub issues. The goal is to make it extra easy for engineers to find
the fix PR link (instead of asking them to hunt through the issue
timeline).

The PR link isn't easily retrievable in GitHub agentic workflows, as the
agent runs in a "read-only" sandbox and can't create the PR itself. It
only **requests** for the PR to be created (via a "safe output"), the PR
is created afterwards so we don't have access to its link. We have no
way to reference it ahead of time.

To work around this, the PR defines a new `link_fix_pr` tool (backed by
a follow-up _job_) that the agent calls after opening a PR. The job runs
after the `safe_outputs` step once both the PR and the comment exist.

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

@@ -100,6 +100,49 @@ safe-outputs:
     # transport makes the shallow safe_outputs checkout run `git fetch --unshallow`,

+  # Adds the fix PR's URL to the outcome comment. The agent can't do this itself:
+  # it doesn't know the PR number while it runs (safe_outputs creates the PR
+  # afterwards), so this job runs after safe_outputs and edits the just-posted comment.
+  jobs:
+    link-fix-pr:
+      description: 'Append the newly-opened fix PR''s URL to the outcome comment on the issue. Call this exactly once, and only after you have opened a draft PR.'
+      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+      needs: safe_outputs
+      if: needs.safe_outputs.outputs.created_pr_url != '' && needs.safe_outputs.outputs.comment_id != ''
+      permissions:
+        issues: write
+      inputs:
+        confirm:
+          description: 'Set to true to append the opened fix PR link to the outcome comment. Only call this after a PR has been opened.'

+        # The URL of the fix PR that safe_outputs just created (the link to add).

+        GH_AW_COMMENT_ID: ${{ needs.safe_outputs.outputs.comment_id }}

[Flaky Test Fixer] Isolate concurrency group per label event (#280437)

I noticed the Flaky Test Fixer didn't open a fix PR for issue #280294 —
the `ai:fix-flaky` label was applied but nothing ran, and the label was
never cleared.

Upon further investigation, it looks like the investigator applied
`ai:fix-flaky` in the same batch as its `failure:*` classification
labels, and all of those label events ran on the same concurrency "lane"
(keyed only on the issue number). GitHub keeps only one pending run per
lane, so the sibling `failure:*` events — which do nothing but skip —
bumped the only valid trigger (`ai:fix-flaky`) out of the pending slot
and [cancelled it before any job
started](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/actions/runs/29971327890).
This PR computes a different lane name for non-`ai:fix-flaky` label
events so they won't override the real trigger.

The fix mirrors what we already do in the Failed Test Investigator
(#274141): give unrelated label events their own concurrency lane
(suffixed by the label name) so they skip harmlessly. `ai:fix-flaky`
events (and `workflow_dispatch`) keep sharing one `-fix` lane per issue
so duplicate requests still serialize, and `job-discriminator` scopes
the generated conclusion job per issue.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
